items.context: A text message to a friend before a trip

items.prompt: Our flight leaves at six, so we need to ___ at the airport by four.

explanation.en: At an airport we check in, that is, register for the flight. Check out is for leaving a hotel.

items.prompt: I'll pick you up at three if the traffic ___ too bad.

explanation.en: In a first conditional the if-clause takes the present simple, not will.
explanation.es: En la oración con «if» se usa el presente simple, no «will».

items.prompt: Don't forget your passport, because you ___ travel without it.

explanation.en: Mustn't means it is forbidden. Don't have to and needn't mean it is not necessary.
explanation.es: «Mustn't» es prohibición; «don't have to» es «no hace falta».

items.prompt: The hotel is only ten minutes ___ foot from the beach, so we can walk down every morning.

explanation.en: The fixed phrase is on foot. We use by for vehicles, such as by bus.

items.prompt: Send me a message as soon as you ___ in Lisbon.

explanation.en: Arrive in a city is correct. Reach takes a direct object (reach Lisbon) and go needs to.
